events.title: Ornament is required
events.text: Antonym read “Ornament is crime” and concluded that the crime was having too little of it. Pilasters, rosettes, garlands, gold, onion domes: Loos's white cube has never been so decorated.

events.title: Less? More!
events.text: “Less is more,” Mies said. Antonym heard “Less? More!” and kept adding: rooms on rooms, roofs on roofs, chimneys, flags, columns and garden gnomes. The glass pavilion is gone under all of it.

daemons.name: Paraphrase
daemons.creed: Retells every idea in its own words, which mean the opposite.

events.title: Doing less with more
events.text: Fuller's dome did more with less. Paraphrase retold it as “doing less with more”: a solid concrete dome, eight buttresses, a plinth, and one tiny door you have to crawl through.

events.title: Emptiness is wasted space
events.text: “It is the emptiness at the centre that makes the wheel useful.” Paraphrase thought that emptiness was simply wasted space, so it filled the whole wheel solid and piled everything it could find on top.

events.title: A machine, literally
events.text: “A house is a machine for living in.” Literal took him at his word: Villa Savoye now has wheels, gears, pistons, rivets, smokestacks and a giant wind-up key on the roof.

events.title: The curves returned to God
events.text: “The straight line belongs to men, the curved line to God.” Literal decided the curves had to be given back. Every wave, arch and spire has been straightened into grey boxes.

daemons.name: Typo
daemons.creed: Misreads exactly one word, every time.

events.title: Function follows form
events.text: Typo swapped two words: “function follows form.” So the form came first, upside down. The cornice sits on the ground, the shops hang 30 metres up, and the front door is reached by ladder.

events.title: Less is a box
events.text: “Less is a bore,” wrote Venturi. Typo read “less is a box” and delivered exactly that: one white box with no windows, no gable and no chimney. The sign out front now says I AM A BOX.

events.title: Only right angles
events.text: “There are 360 degrees, so why stick to one?” Footnote skipped to the footnote, which says 90 of them are right angles, and rebuilt the flowing shell out of cubes.

events.title: Never repeat a maxim
events.text: Kant: act only on a maxim you could will to be universal. Footnote found a note saying “no two cases are alike” and rebuilt the nine identical houses so that none resembles another.
